posts.title: Two envelopes at the window
posts.excerpt: Noor came to the Ghent shop, held two plain envelopes to the window, and left with Soft Wove.
posts.content:
Noor came to the shop on Papierstraat with a letter that was not finished. She did not ask for a kind of pen, and she did not ask us to name a favourite sheet. She asked to see the envelopes in the window light. The letter had to leave Ghent, and she wanted to know how the paper would look once it was held up.

Aya Mensah was at the counter. She put two plain envelopes in Noor’s hands and nodded at the glass. One was white. The other was a pale kraft. Noor raised them both. Daylight went through the paper, and the difference was easy to see without a talk about it. This is the first step we use with anyone. Feel comes before cut, and cut comes before wrap. The window does the feeling.

The sheet on the table was Soft Wove. It is A4, 120 gsm, fifty sheets in a pack, €13. We keep it for fountain pens. The plain envelopes are the same weight, 120 gsm, in C6. A pack holds twenty-five and costs €8. One A4 sheet, folded twice, fits that envelope. Noor set a sheet of Soft Wove behind each envelope in turn. The white one kept the letter close to the page she was writing. The kraft one warmed it. She chose the white. Both envelopes are the same pack. We do not sell a second envelope at a second price.

She did not need the rest of the range for this letter, and Aya said so. Airmail Bank is the 45 gsm sheet for long letters abroad. Everyday Bond is the 80 gsm sheet for daily writing and printing. Laid Writing is the 100 gsm sheet for letters by hand, the one that shows chain lines when you hold it to the light. Grey Card is the 250 gsm sheet for cards and backing. Cotton Rag is the 300 gsm sheet for watercolour and invitations. Soft Wove is only the fountain-pen sheet. The plain envelope only takes one A4 folded twice. Noor was matching a letter to packs we already keep, not building a set.

Joris Van Acker was at the mat that morning. Samples are cut through the morning after the door opens at 10:00. Noor did not need a cut. The A4 sheet and the C6 envelope already agreed. If the job had been a card, Grey Card could have been cut to size for nothing. If it had been an invitation smaller than A3, Cotton Rag could have been cut the same way. Cutting to size is free, and so is the kraft wrap tied with cotton tape. A sheet that has been cut cannot be returned. An unopened pack can, within thirty days.

She took one pack of Soft Wove at €13 and one pack of plain envelopes at €8. Together that sits under €60, so a posted order would have carried the flat €7 inside the EU, or €16 elsewhere. She did not post it. She was already in the shop. Ravi Nair handles the orders that do leave by the web. Tomás Rivera wraps those parcels. A pack that goes into a bag at the counter does not need the tape. Parcels that do leave go out at 16:30.

Aya Paper was founded in 2011 in Ghent. The shop is at 17 Papierstraat, 9000 Ghent. Tuesday to Saturday the door is open from 10:00 to 18:00. Noor came while there was still daylight to hold paper in, which is the point of doing this at the window rather than under a lamp in a back room. On Thursday, from 16:00 to 18:00, Greta Lindholm holds the paper clinic for someone who has brought a sample and is not sure which of the six sheets to use. Noor was sure once she had looked. She did not need the clinic.

Aya did not add a second recommendation on the way out. The range stops at six papers because each one has a job, and another paper would repeat a job we can already name at the counter. Leila Benali buys those papers from the mills. She does not bring in a sheet we cannot explain in one sentence. Soft Wove’s sentence is that it is for fountain pens. The envelope’s sentence is that it takes one A4 folded twice.

Noor put the packs in her bag. The letter was still unfinished. That was fine. The shop does not write the letter. Hanna Kowalczyk would stitch notebooks at 14:00, and the day’s parcels would leave at 16:30, and none of that changed the reason for the visit. Noor had stood at the window with two envelopes and one sheet, and she had chosen.

posts.title: A thesis on Everyday Bond
posts.excerpt: Bram in Leuven printed a whole thesis on the plain bond.
posts.content:
Bram is finishing a thesis in Leuven and prints each draft at home. He tried several papers and settled on Everyday Bond (80 gsm, A4, 250 sheets, €12) because it feeds through a home printer without jamming and takes pencil notes in the margin.

He buys a pack every few weeks and says the square-cut edges stack neatly in a folder. For the final copy he asked for a few sheets of Laid Writing, which the shop cut to size on the mat.

Web orders like his are dispatched in 2 working days, and delivery over €60 is free.

posts.title: Forty invitations, one sheet at a time
posts.excerpt: Sofia and Dan in Antwerp cut forty invitations from Cotton Rag.
posts.content:
Sofia and Dan wanted invitations that felt like something to keep. They chose Cotton Rag (300 gsm, A3, 10 sheets, €24), which has a deckle edge on every side, and asked the counter to cut each A3 sheet down to size.

Cutting forty cards takes a steel rule, a sharp knife and patience. Joris did the first few with them, then they finished the rest at home, one sheet at a time.

The stack travelled to Antwerp wrapped in kraft paper and tied with cotton tape.

posts.title: Weight is not thickness
posts.excerpt: A short note from Leila Benali on what gsm tells you and what it does not.
posts.content:
Leila Benali buys the six papers from the mills, and the question she hears most is which one is thickest. Weight is the figure on the pack, in grams per square metre. It tells you how much a square metre of the sheet weighs, not how thick it is.

Two papers of the same weight can feel different in the hand, because the fibres, the pressing and the finish change how much room the sheet takes. That is why the counter asks you to hold the sheets to the window before you choose.

The shop keeps six papers so the comparison stays in the hand: Airmail Bank at 45 gsm up to Cotton Rag at 300 gsm.

products.name: Airmail Bank
products.short: A thin, translucent sheet for long letters abroad.
products.description:
Airmail Bank is 45 gsm, A4, 100 sheets, €9. The surface is thin and translucent, and a stack shows fanned edges when you lift it. It is for long letters abroad, so the ink on it is the ink of a letter that has to travel, not a sheet we sell for drawing on both sides.

We do not publish a show-through figure. Leave it at A4, or ask for a cut if the letter must be smaller. Joris Van Acker cuts sample sets and finished sizes on the mat. Cutting is free. Paper cut to size cannot be returned. An unopened pack can be returned within 30 days.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Everyday Bond
products.short: Bright white bond for daily writing and printing.
products.description:
Everyday Bond is 80 gsm, A4, 250 sheets, €12. The surface is bright white and the edges are square-cut, so a ream sits flush. It suits daily writing and printing, which is why Bram in Leuven used it for a thesis and why we also point households and small studios to it. Ink here means ordinary writing and ordinary printing.

We do not publish a toner score or an inkjet score. If you need a size other than A4, we cut it at the counter for nothing. Keep the pack unopened if you might send it back. Returns are 30 days, and only on unopened paper.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Laid Writing
products.short: Chain lines you can see in the light, for letters by hand.
products.description:
Laid Writing is 100 gsm, A4, 100 sheets, €14. Held to the light, the chain lines in the laid surface are visible. That surface is why the sheet exists. We keep it for letters by hand, so the ink we expect on it is pen on those lines, not a printed page. Fountain pens have their own sheet, Soft Wove.

We do not publish a bleed test for either. An A4 sheet folds twice into our C6 envelope. If the letter should be smaller still, we cut it on the mat at no charge. A cut sheet stays sold. An unopened pack can come back within 30 days.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Soft Wove
products.short: A faintly warm white sheet for a fountain pen.
products.description:
Soft Wove is 120 gsm, A4, 50 sheets, €13. The surface is a soft wove, faintly warm white, without laid lines. It is the paper we name for fountain pens. The ink has this quieter face rather than the thin airmail sheet, and we still do not quote a dry time or a feathering score.

It suits pen notes and pen letters. At the counter you can hold it to the window beside a plain envelope, which is what Noor did. We cut it when the note is not A4. The cut is free, and cut paper cannot be returned. Unopened packs can, within 30 days.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Grey Card
products.short: Thick grey card with square edges, for cards and backing.
products.description:
Grey Card is 250 gsm, A5, 25 sheets, €11. The surface is grey card with thick, square edges. It suits cards and backing, including thank-you cards and mounting, not a long letter. People write a few words on a card cut from it. We do not treat it as a prose sheet, and we do not publish an ink-density figure.

Many cards can stay A5. If you need another size, Joris cuts it on the mat for nothing. Once it is cut, it cannot be returned. An unopened pack of 25 can be returned within 30 days. The kraft wrap, if you are posting cards, is free.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Cotton Rag
products.short: Cotton rag with deckle edges, for watercolour and invitations.
products.description:
Cotton Rag is 300 gsm, A3, 10 sheets, €24. The surface is cotton rag and the edges are deckle, not square. It suits watercolour and invitations. Those are the only two jobs we sell it for. We do not give a soaking time or a weight of water. Sofia and Dan in Antwerp used it for forty invitations, one sheet at a time.

The sheet is A3, so a smaller invitation is a counter cut, and the cut is free. A cut sheet cannot be returned. An unopened pack can be returned within 30 days. Tomás Rivera wraps a flat parcel in kraft paper and cotton tape when the sheets are leaving the shop.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Plain Envelopes
products.short: The only envelope we sell: C6, for one A4 folded twice.
products.description:
Plain Envelopes are 120 gsm, C6, 25 to a pack, at €8. They suit one A4 sheet folded twice. The paper is blank, with no lining, no window and no printed return. In the shop you can fan them on the table or hold two up to the window, one white and one pale kraft, and look at the light through them.

That is how Noor in Ghent chose. The pack is the same item either way. It is not a second envelope with another price. Soft Wove is the A4 sheet we most often set beside them, because both are 120 gsm and the letter inside is often written with a fountain pen. The kraft wrap for a posted pack is free.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.

products.name: Stitched Notebook
products.short: A5, 96 blank pages, stitched in the shop.
products.description:
The Stitched Notebook is 100 gsm, A5, 96 pages, at €16, for everyday notes. Hanna Kowalczyk stitches it in the shop. Stitching is part of the day at 14:00, after the morning samples and before parcels leave at 16:30. The books on the shelf show their spines and the thread. The pages are blank. We do not call the notebook Laid Writing and we do not call it Soft Wove.

Those are separate packs. The notebook simply is 100 gsm, sewn, A5. It is not returnable once the stitching is a special cut or a page has been used. An unopened book can be returned within 30 days, like any unopened pack. Open books used as shop samples stay in the shop.

Free delivery over €60 · Counter wrap free.
